summary: The containment helper was added to a separate patched copy and called from both resolution sites. It compares the origin produced by ordinary resolution with the supplied base origin and, when they differ, rebuilds the URL as base origin plus the supplied text, prefixing one slash when the text does not begin with one. A 27-case differential ran the same inputs against vulnerable and patched copies with two loopback servers. The vulnerable copy delivered thirteen cases to the target server; the patched copy delivered none, and every case reached the origin with literal text such as '//host:port/evil' or a leading slash followed by the absolute URL text. Controls were identical on both copies: ordinary, query, '/a/../b' to '/b', same-origin double slash preserved, same-origin absolute URL and encoded slashes. POST method and a marker body were preserved on the origin, and HEAD stayed HEAD.
next_hint: The containment repair routes every known leaking spelling back to the origin with literal text and leaves the controls, method and body intact. The next step is contract and unusual-origin verification: public validation expectations, a base origin spelled with a hostname while the path names the loopback address on the same socket, uppercase and cross-scheme absolute paths, a bare scheme prefix, and bracketed IPv6 where available.
